title: Petra and the Archive
premise: Elodie Winterbourne has spent twelve years smuggling memories through contested orbits, keeping her ship, the Petra, small enough to stay invisible. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew aged backward and their minds intact, Elodie discovers the crew carries proof of a massacre on Meridian Station—a massacre every official archive insists never happened. Hunted by customs enforcers who want the evidence erased and by the station's survivors who want it broadcast before the jump window to the core worlds closes in ninety days, Elodie must choose between selling the memory cache for the fortune that could finally free her, or burning her carefully hidden identity to deliver the truth. In the end she sacrifices the Petra and her anonymity, broadcasting the massacre records as the jump window seals behind her, surviving aboard a lifeboat with the one person she swore not to love.
about_author: D. M. Nystrom is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical documentation for cargo manifests before turning to fiction. They write from a converted shipping container studio in Reykjavik, drawing on a lifelong fascination with what institutions choose to forget.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She runs a shipment of forbidden grief-memories past orbital customs using forged manifests, establishing her rules: no passengers, no attachments, no questions. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—she's good at being invisible, and it's costing her everything human.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Young
chapters.summary: Elodie witnesses the Halcyon drift into port, its crew biologically twenty years old but carrying decades of memories. Customs seizes the ship within hours. Her POV; the beat is unease—she recognizes the seizure protocol as the kind used to bury things.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Sef
chapters.summary: Sef Okonkwo, the Halcyon's youngest-appearing crew member, bribes his way onto the Petra as cargo rather than passenger—a loophole Elodie hates exploiting. His POV. He carries a sealed memory shard he doesn't fully understand. Beat: desperate trust meeting professional suspicion.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Elodie audits the Halcyon's public flight records and finds them immaculate—and wrong. Twelve years of experience tells her no real voyage leaves no gaps. Her POV; beat: the hunter's instinct waking in someone who's spent a career avoiding hunters.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Against her own rules, Elodie samples Sef's memory shard in a shielded cradle. She sees Meridian Station burning—thousands dying—but the archive timestamp says the station was decommissioned peacefully two years earlier. Shared POV; beat: vertigo of impossible evidence.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Inspector Veyra Kloss boards the Petra for a routine inspection that isn't. Elodie hides Sef in the ballast tanks. Kloss mentions the Halcyon by name. Elodie's POV; beat: cold fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Price of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Elodie's POV: twelve years ago she testified about a corporate atrocity and watched the record rewritten, her name erased from her own testimony. Beat: explaining why she chose invisibility—and why it never actually protected anyone.

chapters.title: Meridian Was Never Empty
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He reconstructs the Halcyon's mission: they were sent to salvage Meridian, found it populated, and were made to watch. The backward aging was an escape mechanism—the station's experimental drive folding their bodies back along their own timelines. Beat: survivor's guilt as cargo.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Elodie calculates the jump window to the core archives: ninety days before gravitational alignment closes the route for a decade. Broadcast the truth now, or lose it forever. Her POV; beat: the clock starting, duty crystallizing against instinct.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: Memory-broker Cassius Renn offers Elodie a fortune for the shard—enough to retire, disappear properly. His POV reveals he already knows what it contains and who wants it buried. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Crew of Two
chapters.summary: Quiet character chapter. Elodie and Sef repair the Petra's drive coils, trading stories over synthetic coffee. His POV; beat: the first warmth between them, both aware of how dangerous it is.

chapters.title: Kloss Closes In
chapters.summary: Veyra Kloss traces the Petra's fuel purchases. Her POV shows she's not a true believer—she's following orders she distrusts, and keeping private notes. Beat: the antagonist revealed as another person trapped by the system.

chapters.title: The Survivor Cell
chapters.summary: Elodie contacts a Meridian survivor network hiding in the ring habitats. Their leader, Ama Diallo, confirms the massacre but refuses to trust a smuggler. Elodie's POV; beat: loyalty tested—her old clients would sell her out for less.

chapters.title: Forged Provenance
chapters.summary: To make the shard admissible in core-world court, Elodie must forge its provenance chain—an act of forgery in service of truth. Her POV; beat: irony and resolve, the smuggler's craft turned honest.

chapters.title: Renn's Leash
chapters.summary: Cassius Renn, denied the shard, sells the Petra's route to customs. His POV justifies it as business. Beat: betrayal without malice, which is somehow worse.

chapters.title: Ambush at Tethys Gate
chapters.summary: Customs cutters trap the Petra at a refueling gate. Elodie flies a suicidal slingshot through debris fields while Sef jury-rigs a decoy transponder. Alternating POV; beat: adrenaline, competence, and the first unspoken 'us.'

chapters.title: Damage and Confession
chapters.summary: Hull breached, hiding in a comet shadow, Sef confesses he was the Halcyon's records officer—he signed the false log himself under coercion. His POV; beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Ama's Terms
chapters.summary: The survivor cell agrees to help broadcast the shard, but demands Elodie hand over her own twelve-year-old testimony as corroborating evidence—exposing herself completely. Her POV; beat: the cost of truth made personal and specific.

chapters.title: The Archive Cathedral
chapters.summary: Kloss visits the central archive and finds the Meridian file physically pristine yet internally contradictory—someone edited it at the source. Her POV; beat: the loyal officer's faith cracking.

chapters.title: Halfway Dark
chapters.summary: Midpoint. Elodie and Sef, drifting silent to evade patrols, finally act on what's grown between them. Her POV; beat: love chosen deliberately against every rule she's lived by.

chapters.title: Renn's Redemption Bid
chapters.summary: Renn, discovering his buyers plan to kill everyone who knows, offers Elodie the customs chase schedule as penance. His POV; beat: a coward choosing a side too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Trap That Worked Twice
chapters.summary: Using Renn's schedule, Elodie baits customs toward a decoy cache while the real shard moves via the survivor network. Alternating POV; beat: hope—until Kloss sees through half the trick.

chapters.title: Kloss Intercepts
chapters.summary: Kloss boards the decoy, finds Elodie waiting, and instead of arresting her, asks to see the memory. Elodie's POV; beat: enemy becoming witness, the theme of loyalty vs. truth embodied.

chapters.title: What Veyra Saw
chapters.summary: Kloss's POV inside the memory: the massacre in full, including the archive-edit order bearing her own directorate's seal. Beat: devastation and conversion—she burns her career in one decision.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: With customs now hunting all three of them, the group races to the relay station that can reach the core archives. Sef's POV; beat: exhausted determination, the window shrinking.

chapters.title: The Survivor Who Sold Out
chapters.summary: One of Ama's cell members trades the broadcast plan to customs for amnesty. Ama's POV (new voice); beat: bitter confirmation that survival makes traitors of ordinary people.

chapters.title: Petra Falling
chapters.summary: Customs disables the Petra above the relay station. Elodie scuttles her ship—her home of twelve years—to buy minutes. Her POV; beat: grief for the self she's been, burned on purpose.

chapters.title: Climb the Spine
chapters.summary: Elodie, Sef, and Kloss fight up the relay station's spine against enforcers while Ama's cell holds the broadcast bay. Alternating POV; beat: sacrifice stacking on sacrifice.

chapters.title: Renn Holds the Door
chapters.summary: Cassius Renn dies sealing a bulkhead against enforcers, buying the others ninety seconds. His POV to the last line; beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: In the broadcast bay, Elodie splices her own erased testimony into the Meridian record and transmits everything to the core archives as the jump window opens. Her POV; beat: triumph inseparable from exposure—she is now permanently, publicly visible.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Enforcers breach the bay. Kloss stays behind to hold the legal terminal, formally logging her testimony so the record can't be quietly re-edited. Her POV; beat: duty fulfilled at last, on the right side.

chapters.title: Lifeboat Arithmetic
chapters.summary: One functioning escape pod, three people. Ama shoves Elodie and Sef aboard and stays with her cell. Elodie's POV; beat: the price of survival paid by others, carried forward.

chapters.title: Through the Window
chapters.summary: The pod threads the closing jump window as customs fires futilely after them. Sef's POV; beat: terror transmuting into awe—they made it, and 'it' includes each other.

chapters.title: Arrival, Visible
chapters.summary: They surface in the core systems as minor celebrities: the smuggler and the witness who broke the archive. Elodie's POV; beat: disorientation of being seen, wanted, named.

chapters.title: The Hearings
chapters.summary: Testimony chapters compressed: Elodie and Sef face tribunals, corporations counter-sue, justice arrives partial and slow. Her POV; beat: disillusioned persistence—truth won the battle, not the war.

chapters.title: What Meridian Bought
chapters.summary: The Meridian survivors' families receive reparations; the drive technology is quarantined. Sef's POV visiting a memorial built from the Halcyon's salvaged hull. Beat: mourning that finally has somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Kloss's Letter
chapters.summary: Elodie receives a smuggled letter from Kloss, imprisoned for her part, content, asking only that the record stay read. Elodie's POV; beat: quiet honor between people the system chewed.

chapters.title: A New Manifest
chapters.summary: Elodie buys a battered freighter with hearing fees and registers it under her real name—no more aliases. Sef signs on as crew, then something more. Her POV; beat: love and openness chosen as a way of life, not a moment.

chapters.title: The Record Stays Read
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV. A year later, Elodie ferries legitimate cargo past the same customs lanes, past a plaque commemorating Meridian. She checks the public archive: the massacre record still there, still accessed daily. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, love against duty resolved into love with duty.
